tasks.short: Examine specimens for abnormal hormonal patterns

steps.what: Read specimen identity and relevant hormonal history before examination
Examine specimens microscopically and assess cellular maturation and specimen quality
Distinguish abnormal hormone patterns from artefacts and clinical confounders
Enter interpreted findings and limitations in the existing examination worksheet
Save the examination worksheet in the laboratory case

tasks.design: Configure the existing {OTHER} laboratory case view to show request and supplied hormonal history together. Keep microscopy, interpretation and the actual examination worksheet fully manual; only repeated navigation is removed.
tasks.previous_blocker: Relevant request information can sit on separate laboratory screens.
tasks.enabler_now: A native case view can show existing fields together without inferring hormonal status.
tasks.still_hard: Distinguishing cellular maturation patterns from inflammation, treatment effects and inadequate specimens.
tasks.human_edge: The cytotechnologist integrates microscopic appearances with the limits of the available history.
tasks.altitude: A little less screen navigation. Examination and interpretation rights do not change.

reach.learn: Pre-analytical quality and limitations of hormonal history

evidence.claim: A native laboratory case view can group existing request fields; it does not replace microscopic examination or hormonal interpretation.

assumptions: Boundary is examination and its existing worksheet, used in laboratory review. Specimen preparation is unchanged upstream work and no saving is credited there. No new diary, tally or management record is created. A final clinical report or its release is a separate action with no saving claimed here.

The request producer supplies case identifier, specimen identifier, specimen type, collection date and any available hormonal history. The technologist checks identity and reads the supplied history in s1. Missing history is not inferred; clarification and manual retrieval remain in its nine retained hours.

The native view removes one hour of repeated navigation from ten hours of context reading; it does not cut reading or clinical verification. This is an unmeasured scenario estimate. If no repeat navigation exists, retain the present view.

The actual worksheet is already attached to the case and has its headings available. Its nine hours are new observation and limitation entry, so neither a template nor a model gets a saving. Ordinary same-system save time is one hour, fully retained and ungated.

Microscopy uses the {OTHER} microscope category; case viewing and worksheet entry use the {OTHER} laboratory information system. No machine interpretation, inference, clinical release or external send is proposed.
unknowns: Are request and history already visible on one screen?
Which worksheet fields are actually used in local review?
research_questions: Does a combined case view remove repeat navigation while preserving source labels and missing-history flags?

already_counted.description: Identity and context checking, including manual retrieval of unavailable history
Actual observation entry and ordinary save

incremental.description: Recheck the case-view fields after laboratory system changes

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Central: one navigation hour removed, less 0.2 upkeep gives 0.8. Low: hormonal history is absent or already displayed beside the request, so the combined view adds no benefit and is not deployed; existing work remains unchanged.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Spend marginally less time navigating the laboratory case, with unchanged microscopy and interpretation work.
reach: Help laboratory colleagues make specimen context easier to inspect
role.ambitious_version: A cytotechnologist with clearer specimen context and unchanged responsibility for interpreting what the cells show.
